capacity_caption: Each line is the best test error reached by any network at or below that size (best of three seeds). The PID law is fitted by the smallest network tried (17 parameters). Adding a clip to the same law costs about 900× more parameters for 1%, because a smooth network struggles to draw a sharp kink. The camera version starts high because its 1,152 pixel inputs make even the narrowest network 2,300 parameters.
table_caption: Params for x% are interpolated between tested widths; '—' means not reached within 70k parameters (the camera task within 296k). 'Weight bits kept' is the fewest bits per weight, under crude uniform per-tensor quantization, that still held 1% (or 1.25× the float error) on the smallest passing network. 'Bits for 1%' = interpolated parameters for 1% × those bits: an upper estimate of the description the network needed. Examples for 1% come from a separate sweep at width 128; 128 is the smallest size tried, so the true minimum may be lower.
chaos_caption: Minimum parameters to fit the t-step flow map to 10% error. Measured finite-time Lyapunov exponents over the sampled boxes: pendulum median 0.88/s (shear near the separatrix, not chaos); double pendulum median 1.75/s, 90th percentile 3.7/s. From 50 to 400 ms the double pendulum's requirement grows about 18× (≈8/s). A Lipschitz-constant argument (Lipschitz constant growing as e^(λt), network size ∝ (L/ε)^(d/s)) predicts d·λ ≈ 7/s for d = 4, s = 1. At 800 ms, no network up to 70k parameters reached 10% (triangle). At fixed size (70k), the double pendulum's best error grows from 1.8% to 20% over the same horizons, about e^(3.2 t), inside the measured Lyapunov range.
data_caption: Width fixed at 128, training sets from 128 to 32,768 examples, best of two seeds. Smooth low-dimensional functions reach 0.3% with the smallest set tried. The double pendulum and the camera version need hundreds to thousands of examples. For smooth state-input tasks the labels needed carry about as many bits as the network needed: the network's bits ÷ the label bits = 0.7–3.6, with one outlier (pendulum 400 ms at 0.3%: 20). Curves flatten where the width-128 network itself becomes the limit (cart-pole ≈0.8%, double pendulum ≈2.7%): more data cannot buy what the model cannot hold.
findings: The ladder is real and steep. Bits the network needed for 1%: PID ≈ 136 (the formula itself is 96 bits of constants), pendulum ≈ 1.4–3.5k, cart-pole ≈ 75k, camera pendulum ≈ 81k. The double pendulum needed ≈ 150k bits for 3% and did not reach 1% within 70k parameters.

Regularity matters as much as size. A clipped PID has four constants, but a smooth-activation network needs about 15k parameters for 1% because of the kink. That is architecture mismatch, ρ_A, measured: a ReLU network would draw the clip almost exactly.
A physics prior pays. Feeding sin θ and cos θ instead of θ cut the parameters needed by about 2× at 1% and 4× at 0.3%.

Seeing through a camera costs. The same pendulum function, observed as two 24×24 frames, needed about 58× the parameters at 1% (mostly the pixel input layer of an MLP; a convolutional network would pay less) and at least 5× the examples.

Chaos multiplies model size with horizon. For the chaotic double pendulum the size needed for 10% grows about 18× from 50 to 400 ms and exceeds 70k parameters by 800 ms. The regular pendulum stays under 100 parameters. At fixed size, error grows at roughly the Lyapunov rate. Feedback control only needs the short-horizon map, which is why a controller can be small when a forecaster cannot.

Data needed tracks the task; parameters track the task × mismatch. Where the architecture fits (smooth state inputs), the labels needed (examples × outputs × log₂(1/ε)) carry ≈ 0.3–1.4× the bits the network needed. Where it fits badly (kink, raw pixels), weights need 10–40× more bits than the labels do. The ratio is a way to measure ρ_A, and the first calibration of the calculator's data line.
limits: One architecture (2-hidden-layer SiLU MLP), one optimizer recipe, 4,000 steps, best of three seeds: every minimum is attained, not proven. Data are noise-free synthetic samples from uniform boxes; the smallest data set tried (128) floors easy tasks. Quantization is crude uniform per-tensor. 'Not reached' is not 'impossible'. This is a small, reproducible demonstration, not a scaling law for vehicles.
